Sometime at the beginning of October, Colonel Sartre, the commander of the French battalion in UNPROFOR, informed me there would be a tripartite meeting which General Morillon wished to organise. I told Colonel Sartre then that I was firmly convinced that the position held of my chief of staff would be that prior to any kind of tripartite meeting, a meeting should be held between representatives of the HVO and representatives of the BH army so as to coordinate their views and agree on the stand they would take. I informed the chief of staff, Brigadier Petkovic, of this, and Brigadier Petkovic designated to that delegation myself. He was there, and several officers from the main staff, and Ignac Kostroman. We were designated by the head of the delegation, the chief of staff of the HVO. Before the meeting which was organised by General Morillon, in the building of the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Sarajevo, we met with high-ranking officials of the Bosniak Muslims, politicians as well as military man, I think they were led by Mr. Ejub Ganic, Sefer Halilovic, and Stjepan Siber. After that meeting and an agreement reached on the stand we would take, we went to the airport in Sarajevo to attend a tripartite meeting. Mr. Kordic was appointed subsequently to be a member of that delegation. When Travnik was attacked, this was sometime in November 1992, and when, due to the military situation, I was unable to attend those meetings. So Kordic did attend those meetings when I was unable to go because the town of Travnik was being threatened. The Serbs knew when these meetings were being held, and their combat operations, in most cases, coincided with the timing of these meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you a document, General.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 628, 628A for the English version, Prosecutor's Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's take a look at this document, General. This is a document that's sent in the packet system; isn't it? Did you hear my question, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was reading the document, so I didn't hear your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My question is: This is a document that is set on the packet system; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It was sent by packet link, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We do not have a French copy, unfortunately, Mr. President, so I will read it slowly in English. There is, of course, a B/C/S copy for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, 10 November 1992, 22.00. Forward command post. This is sent to Mostar, Grude via Bugojno and Gornji Vakuf. HVO commander in chief or chief of defence department. Report on the proposal for a meeting to: "1. In relation to the talks that General Morillon had with the representatives of the Serbian side, official invitation issued for a meeting with the top level HVO politicians as soon as possible. "2. Serbian proposal, 11 November, 1992, at Sarajevo airport or wherever we propose in Central Bosnia, Kiseljak, Busovaca, Vitez. "3. Representative on the Serbian side is Mr. Koljevic. "4. Subject of talk: Immediate ceasefire in Mostar. I propose that our side is represented by president of Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Mr. Dario Kordic, and secretary, Ignac Kostroman. "5. I am asking you to send the authorisation or approval on attending the meeting or should we refuse. "6. Chairman is General Morillon. "7. I must have the reply by 09.00 on 11 November '92 and delivered to General Morillon. "Commander Tihomir Blaskic." Hand-written on the left-hand side is: "Received on 10 November, 1992 at 23.55," and some initials thereafter. Did you send this, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course, and it could be seen here that I had a talk. I know for certain that on the 5th of November I attended a meeting in Sarajevo. I was there before that, beginning with the 23rd of October, 1992, at all the tripartite meetings held by General Morillon as the chairman of the meeting. The meetings always had their topics, and I always represented the Croatian Defence Council, including the 5th of November, 1992. I believe that as it states here, on the basis of the talks with General Morillon that this invitation for a meeting arose. The information that I received from the General, I sent them to Mostar, and here it says via Gornji Vakuf and so on and so forth. I sent them off, and you can see this from point 2 and 3 the information that I received and the topic of the conversation. I made a proposal as to who could take part. I don't know whether my proposal -- I can't remember whether my proposal was accepted or not, and as we were dealing here with a meeting to be held in the Central Bosnia region, for technical organisational purposes, I suggested that these individuals be present. Kostroman had been a participant at all the tripartite meetings held up until then chaired by General Morillon. I stated, at the meeting, General Morillon would indeed be chairman and that he would like an answer by 9.00 on the 11th of November and that I was to convey it to General Morillon. I believe that on the 12th of November, because the meetings were held every seven days, that on the 12th of November in Sarajevo a tripartite meeting was indeed held, chaired by General Morillon or perhaps Brigadier-General Cordy-Simpson, because if General Morillon was absent Crody-Simpson would be the official.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, going back to my initial question, after you learned that Kostroman and Kordic wanted to establish HVO control in these municipalities, after you knew that that was their political agenda, you, nonetheless, nominated them to go to the meetings. So when you told this Court that you didn't, you, in fact, did; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is not correct. You asked me a question linked to who had nominated Mr. Kostroman to attend the meetings, as I understood them, in Sarajevo, and Mr. Kordic. This is a proposal, not an appointment. Apart from that, Kostroman, as I told the Trial Chamber, attended meetings from the 23rd of October, 1992, but not appointed by me but by appointment of the chief of the main staff. I did not put him forward at that time and appoint him. Therefore, he was already at those meetings and there are documents to testify to that. Here Mr. Koljevic is not a soldier. Had we told it that it would have been General Gvero, I would have proposed that it be a military participant of the meeting, that is to say, somebody from the military part of the HVO. This was also a time when the meetings were being held in Sarajevo with all the parties and the time when the joint command was functioning. It was November 1992 when the joint command was functioning on the basis of a decision by Mr. Bozo Rajic, the Defence Minister. This joint command was made up of Mr. Pasalic and Mr. Prakcin for Central Bosnia. I know that they had good co-operation with the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, let me turn your attention back to Exhibit 495/95 and look at the area that says: "Observations noted in all municipalities." This, of course, is the document executed by Kostroman, Valenta, and Kordic. Do you see that section, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I see that section on page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Look about halfway through and I'll read it to you. About halfway through and I'll read it to you. The document from the working presidency of which you were a part and executed by Kostroman, Valenta, and Kordic. "Exiled B and H, Bosnia and Herzegovina government and its bodies with pro-Muslim policies are undesirable on our territory, and their possible activity contrary to the principles of the HDZ bodies shall not be tolerated." This, General, was the political position of which you were aware when you nominated, and I emphasise "nominated," Kostroman and Kordic to go to this meeting with General Morillon; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was not an official political stand. That is what it says here, but in practice this did not -- was not true, because this is a document from -- dated September, and the Ministry of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina held a press conference in Busovaca. I think it was on the 3rd of November, 1992, and then there were other officials. The Prime Minister of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I think, was either Mile Akmadzic or Jure Pelivan. So from the ranks of the Croatian people. Then I would also like to say that there were officials such as Mr. Franjo Boras who took part, and he was at the meeting here as well as a guest, in the capacity of a guest. He is a member of the supreme command of armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and he's also a member of the wartime presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is what it says here in the section that you read out. But in fact, in the field, the situation was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, let's stay with Franjo Boras. Franjo Boras was an advocate of the severance of Bosnia-Herzegovina and its absorption into the Republic of Croatia, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know his political activities for me to be able to give an opinion. I'm talking about the times when I was present at the meeting attended by Franjo Boras as well, and I recall very well what he said on the 26th of March, 1993 in Zenica, for example. It is not what he followed. The complete political activity of Franjo Boras's presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I don't know the details. I had very little contact with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you're well aware of Mr. Boras's meetings with the Serb side of the Bosnian presidency, Mr. Koljevic, where they hatched a plan for the severance of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the transplanting of the Muslim population out of their respective areas. You're aware of that; aren't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That Franjo Boras had a meeting with Nikola Koljevic. I had no information of that kind particularly at the time. Perhaps there were meetings of that kind, but I'd like to underline once again that I had official information and official stands, and possibly meetings of that kind did occur but I had no knowledge of them and Franjo Boras never told me about activities of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We'll come back to the politics of Franjo Boras later. Let us just complete our analysis of this transcript, General. We're talking about Kostroman's speech on the 16th of January. He says, toward the end of this speech: "I would like to stress just one more thing as we see it. Perhaps there will not be any conflict in our areas if we succeed reaching agreements as brothers, if one may say, so fortify the boarders of the state of Croatia in a peaceful way. If we do not succeed, you understand that the boarders of every state will have to be defended and so will these borders. We are the best guarantee to defend them." Now, based on that, General, do you assume that Kostroman was advocating military action to defend the decision or the goal to make Central Bosnia part of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, first of all, you are talking about a decision. It was an individual statement, and he said, "I claim," "I maintain." So it is his personal statement. Secondly, I can comment on what I assume he had in mind, because at the time the Yugoslav People's Army, located in the area, was the sole armed force in Bosnia-Herzegovina. So he could have sent that kind of message both to the Yugoslav People's Army and to its components, as well as to the members of all the others who were opposed to that personal idea of his. But as far as I know, it was not an official stand, an official idea. That idea was not handed down to me through the system of command from my superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, you talk about official ideas. Let's be very clear. When you were in Central Bosnia, what was Kordic's duties and responsibilities as a political officer, political official?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really don't know what they were. If you are asking me about my own, I would be very ready to answer you, but the duties that he performed I don't know. I know that he was the vice-president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and that he was a member of the HDZ party. He was at one time its vice-president, but what his duties were as a vice-president I don't know. I never attended party meetings, nor was I a member of the party, and I cannot say what his duties were. I know my own duties full well, but what his were I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we can take a break now if you so choose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. It's very convenient. A 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. We shall resume our work.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise. Could I just make a brief comment as regards 628, Prosecutor's Exhibit 628, because I have read through it in its entirety during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please go ahead, General Blaskic. Six hundred and twenty-eight, you said. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. From point 1 of this document, it is visible that General Morillon is sending out an invitation for a meeting with top-level politicians and that the topic is the ceasefire in Mostar and that the proposal -- that from the Serbian side, Mr. Koljevic would be taking part, he was the vice-president at the time, and probably that is why I suggested to the competent authorities that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna be represented by the deputy, Dario Kordic, which is on a political par with Koljevic, he is his counterpart. I should also like to say that it was a meeting to be chaired or which should have been chaired by General Morillon and that I was to have received an answer in the course of the night, on the 12th of November, in fact, for that meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, General Blaskic. The Trial Chamber is happy to hear you bring these details to its attention. It does seem important for your defence. Mr. Kehoe, are we going on to another subject or are you staying on that particular issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just a few more questions on this issue, and I would like to follow up on a statement that the General made concerning public statements by Mr. Kordic and Kostroman concerning potentially racist or ethnic matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Is it your testimony, General -- well, let me rephrase that question. Did you ever hear Dario Kordic make any public statements denigrating the people of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Never. I think in all these questions, it is difficult for me to pinpoint the time because we are talking about January '92 and September and November, and there were a lot of events in Bosnia-Herzegovina which were taking place and which affected the statements of local politicians and others. I heard that he was perhaps speaking in a more inflammatory way against perhaps the officials or leadership of the Muslims or Bosniaks and possibly he did at times make unnecessary statements which had a bit of what you mentioned a moment ago and that I heard something similar. But his statements were not for me, as I say, binding. What was binding for me were orders from the chief of the main staff and the official documents of the community, but I did not see any racist approach, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, did you ever hear him make statements along the lines that "Bosnia and Herzegovina will cease to exist"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, that is the problem, in fact. Which Bosnia-Herzegovina? You see, on the 16th of January, 1992, it did cease to exist, but the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina ceased to exist within the formation of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and that was a process and, as such, it did cease to exist, and a referendum was called and the state called the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina continued. So perhaps the statements were along those lines. I don't know what time period you actually have in mind, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kehoe. Try to be more precise. When you want to demonstrate something, try to, you know, go directly to the aim you want to reach. If you have one fact you want to put to the witness, just tell it to the witness. You must know that Mr. Kordic, for example, was saying such and such, the witness will say "Yes" or "No," and then you can refer him to a document; otherwise, we are going to lose a lot of time. Let's try to move forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I will just present a document at this time.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Prosecution Exhibit 629, 629A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, this is a press release by the Party of Democratic Action, the SDA, in Vitez, dated 2 February, 1993, signed by the Executive Board of Vitez -- we can place this on the ELMO, if you can? Thank you. I'll read it as follows: "In an interview with Dario Kordic, the vice-president of the so-called Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, aired on HZ Herceg-Bosna TV for Studio Vitez on 1 February, 1993, it was stated among other things that both the Muslims and Bosnia and Herzegovina will cease to exist. "Dario Kordic's statement comes precisely at a time when we are investing great efforts to overcome all problems by peaceful means and when concrete talks are being held on the establishment of a joint government and single MUP, Ministry of Interior, and it jeopardises the course of the talks. "The Muslim people of the Vitez municipality are embittered by this statement which reminds them of an identical statement made at one time by the war criminal, Radovan Karadzic, in the BH parliament. "We will forward this statement to foreign news agencies and the relevant UN bodies so as to show who is provoking the hostilities in Central Bosnia. "We call on the Croatian people to distance themselves publicly from such inflammatory statements by their extremists in order to be able to continue building a joint life and communal spirit of these two peoples in this area." Signed Executive Board of the Vitez SDA, and the date is, of course, 2 February, 1993. Now, General, you would agree with me that these are particularly inflammatory statements by Kordic in saying that "the Muslims and Bosnia-Herzegovina will cease to exist"; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Allow me to read the document because I never had occasion to see this document before, so if I may read it? And I was not in the area of Vitez in February 1993. I don't remember the question. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The question is that this statement by Kordic, "that both the Muslims and Bosnia and Herzegovina will cease to exist," is a very inflammatory statement, is it not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, this statement, which was apparently made in February 1993, that is, at the time of the January conflicts, is certainly a statement causing concern among those who heard it, but from this document, one can see the vast differences there were and the turmoil. While there was a conflict in Busovaca, there were talks in Vitez on the formation of a joint government and a unified MUP. These must have been talks between the Croats and the Muslims in the immediate neighbourhood of the municipality in which a conflict was ongoing between the HVO and the BH army, that is the municipality of Busovaca. I was in Kiseljak at that time, cut off and under siege, but I did attend this meeting at the UN base, and I can only comment on what I read in this statement. If that is what was said, that both would disappear, certainly it is not a well-intentioned statement, but there is no official document which would show that this was the official position of the HVO nor did I receive any orders in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, this statement, "that Bosnia and Herzegovina will cease to exist," is consistent with Kordic's prior statements and Kostroman's statements concerning the division of Bosnia in making a part of Central Bosnia as a part of Croatia; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is a rather complex question, Mr. President, Your Honours. We viewed a videotape dated 16 January, '92, when the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina had still not been formed, so we skipped over a period in which the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina was formed. I am not very familiar with this nor am I an expert, but I know that the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina was proclaimed by referendum. Then there was the period when the authentic military forces committed aggression, and now we are going on to the January conflict of 1993, the signing of a ceasefire between the HVO and the BH army, and a statement which I see here for the first time on this piece of paper and which I am asked to comment on and to draw conclusions from. So very large leaps forward are being made, and the political, state, and military situation was changing from the situation where there was no state of Bosnia-Herzegovina, then a period of excellent cooperation, and then the period of conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. I share the opinion of the witness there. One has to be careful when we compare various excerpts from a different context, political, military and so on. So it is rather delicate to list one after another as if they followed in sequence. You have other documents, Mr. Prosecutor? We're still dealing with the political arena, are we not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We're still talking about what you consider, you the Prosecution, consider to be the political beliefs of the witness as regards the secessionist tendencies, so please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, let us talk about, and we'll move back to the time frame in January of 1992, subsequent to the meeting, and shortly after you arrived back or several months before you arrived back in Central Bosnia, and I ask you to take another look at another document, and I also ask you, when you're looking at this document, and I also ask you, when you're looking at this document, to see if one of the attendees was, in fact, Josip Boro, the man that you first met in the Kiseljak municipality when you returned in April. If I can give you this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Prosecutor's Exhibit 630, 630A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, this is a document which is the excerpts from the minutes dated 27 January, 1992, from a meeting of the Travnik subregional community of Herceg-Bosna. It is signed by Dario Kordic and Ignac Kostroman, and is one of the attendees from Kislejak Josip Boro? Take a look at the front page there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If you're sure of that, there's no point in asking the witness. We see that Josip Boro, president of the Kiseljak municipal assembly, was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So let's not waste time. You know, you will run out of time in the end. You should say that, "We note that Mr. Josip Boro participated in that meeting," and then you go on to your question. If the witness challenges that, that's another matter. So please go on to your question now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Josip Boro, he was the person that you first met with when you came back to Kiseljak in the second week of April of 1992; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. He held the position of president of the municipal assembly of Kiseljak. He was president of parliament of Kiseljak municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, I direct your attention on this document to the bottom of page 2 and the top of page 3. I will read it, as it's not in French.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Usher. That would be paragraph 2 in the English version. Down a little bit. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It reads as follows: "The Presidency of Herceg-Bosna is asked to proclaim the Bosnia and Herzegovina assembly decision on the referendum illegitimate because it does not reflect the actual attitude of the Croatian people in these areas and to hold a referendum for the citizens of Herceg-Bosna about their wish to join the Croatian areas to the Republic of Croatia and this is recommended for the Posavina Croatian community." Counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I apologise to my learned friend but, Mr. President, I think we again have a problem with the translation. That is one point. I have another. Namely, it was translated into Croatian that the Presidency of Herceg-Bosna is requesting that the referendum be proclaimed illegal, but in the original it says that these people are asking the Presidency of Herceg-Bosna to proclaim this referendum illegal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's what it says, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, but the Croatian interpretation that reached me was different. Another point I wish to make, I would suggest that the witness be given time to look through the document and only then should we go on to questions, because a document has to be reviewed in its entirety rather than in abstracts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, this particular methodology was employed by the Defence counsel all through the direct-examination, highlighting particular points that the Defence wanted to discuss. At this particular point, if the witness wants to review every document, we will be here for awhile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You are conducting the cross-examination, but could the booth retranslate the disputed paragraph? I suppose that the booth has the text in Serbo-Croatian. Could we have the Serbo-Croatian text and have it retranslated on the basis of the original? Perhaps Mr. Nobilo could read it to us, this paragraph. Will you read it slowly?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I can read it and it is hardly legible. "It is requested of the presidency of Herceg-Bosna to proclaim the assembly decision of Bosnia-Herzegovina on a referendum as being illegitimate because it doesn't represent the real view of the Croatian people in these areas and that a referendum be called at which the citizens of Herceg-Bosna would state their views regarding joining the Banovina Croatian parts to the Republic of Croatia, and this is also recommended for the Posavina Croatian community."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: "Banovina" is the word used? Was the word "Banovina" used? I heard the word "Banovina." Is that what you read? I'm asking the booth. The interpreters heard the word "Banovina."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, yes. At one point mention is made of "Banovina." It is stated: "Of the Banovina Croatian parts of the Republic of Croatia." That is parts belonging to the Banovina. At the end, the same is recommended to the Posavina Croatian community. That is the Croatian community in the north of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nobilo. I think perhaps that by now the witness has reviewed the text. General Blaskic, I will ask the Prosecutor to put his question to you.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I have, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please go ahead, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we'll get this translation corrected because, obviously, the translation is not complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, when you met Josip Boro in early April -- excuse me, the second week of April of 1992, did he inform you that he had represented the interests of the Kiseljak area at meetings such as this where they are advocating joining this Banovina? Did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He did not inform me about those matters. I have never seen this document before. I was never familiar with such a request dated the 27th of January, 1992. At that time, I was not in Central Bosnia and, personally, in those days, I did not know Josip Boro. I can see here that this regional Travnik community is addressing such a request but, as far as I know, the referendum was a valid matter and, as far as I know, this request was not implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So your testimony is that Josip Boro never told you that his desire, at least, was for Central Bosnia to join with the Republic of Croatia? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You asked me a question in relation to this document. Maybe I didn't understand you properly. Josip Boro did not convey to me personally any information about his participation in a meeting of this kind, nor did I hear anything from Josip Boro linked to this document. Also, regarding the questions of joining to the Republic of Croatia, I don't know which period we are talking about, but I'm trying to recollect. I cannot remember Josip Boro talking to me about these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The period that we are talking about is when you came to Central Bosnia in April of 1992 until you were made the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone on the 27th of June of 1992. During that period, did Josip Boro tell you about what his political aims were and about his goal of joining Central Bosnia to the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: To me personally, I cannot recollect. I can't remember that Josip Boro spoke about those things at the time he was president of the municipal crisis staff and of the municipal assembly of Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So to summarise your contact with these political leaders, Josip Boro never told you about his desire for Central Bosnia to join Croatia, and neither did Kordic, and neither did Kostroman. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I claim that in this period that you have indicated, I never got any official information from them, nor do I know that that was the official position. When I say "official position," I imply official documents published by the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and those that were binding upon me as the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, how about unofficial comments from these three men?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already said that there were statements. We watched today that in January '92 there were radical, emotional, and very sharp-toned statements, but these were various statements at different periods of political, military, and other events in the territory of the former Yugoslavia. Perhaps that is the best description for this period we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I would note, Mr. President, just for the sake of completeness, that on the attendance list, Ante Sliskovic attended this particular meeting as well. With the Court's permission, if I could possibly just go into private session to discuss some testimony that was taken in closed session, I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. I am explaining for the benefit of the public gallery that testimony was taken in closed session and we have to protect that testimony again and, for that reason, we are going into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 9 (redacted) 10 (redacted) 11 (redacted) 12 (redacted) 13 (redacted) 14 (redacted) 15 (redacted) 16 (redacted) 17 (redacted) 18 (redacted) 19 (redacted) 20 (redacted) 21 (redacted) 22 (redacted) 23 (redacted) 24 (redacted) 25 (redacted) redacted page 21103 (private session) redacted page 21104 – private session redacted page 21105 – private session

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could put Prosecutor's Exhibit 572/1 back on the ELMO? If we can pan back on that just a little bit? Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, if you could, could you point out Anto Valenta in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this is Mr. Anto Valenta (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just for the record, Mr. President, Anto Valenta was an attendee at the meeting on the 27th of January, 1992, that is depicted in Exhibit 630.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, tell us, General, what were Anto Valenta's views on the removal of Muslims from land that he believed should be controlled by the Croats?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that perhaps earlier on, before the beginning of the war conflicts in Bosnia-Herzegovina, he wrote a book, and in that book, he presented some of his views which he formulated in the following manner: How to avoid conflicts and war and how to decide upon the division and he had his own approach to the question linked to the division of, so to say, along with avoidance of a conflict, that is, an agreed-upon division, but I also know that the official stands were not a reflection of those personal views, as far as I know. He performed different duties, he was coordinator, he was prime minister of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. He spanned a wide range of duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, he advocated a position that he called "humane resettlement"; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he personally advocated that position and he published that in his book, and I do believe that the book was published before the war broke out in Bosnia-Herzegovina, perhaps at the beginning of 1992 but I'm not quite sure. I personally did not discuss those matters with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, explain to the Judges this concept of "humane resettlement." What are we talking about here?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was not my conception for me to be able to know about it fully, but I know that Valenta published this concept in his book and they were his views, and according to him, it meant the resettlement of a certain section of the population from one area to another with the aim of avoiding a war. That is how he formulated it, at least, in that book of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This particular policy was a policy that came down to Central Bosnia from Dr. Franjo Tudjman, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know where the idea came from. Probably he cited the literature that he used to help him write his book. I don't know where he got the affinity from as a technologist and engineer of technology, why he delved in demography, whether that was an affinity of his or what it was, but I have no information that this idea came to him. Perhaps it did, but I personally have no information as to that, whether the idea came from Dr. Franjo Tudjman or from somebody else, and let me also say in passing that I have not read any book by Dr. Franjo Tudjman and I have no information of the kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you were present when Valenta publicly articulated this position, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Valenta articulated his positions in front of various officials. I remember I was present on one occasion, but I don't remember all the details of what he said. They were his views, they were quite certainly not my own views as he presented and articulated them, and Valenta later on did not take part in the press conferences but organised his own press conferences as a civilian official of the powers that be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, one of the Defence witnesses, Martin Bell, testified, did he not, that Valenta publicly articulated this humane resettlement view at a press conference where you were in attendance. Do you recall his testimony in that regard?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: For reference purposes, counsel, I'm referring to pages 17619 through 17621.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not only did he publicly articulate those views, quite possibly on that occasion I doubt that that was so. He wrote the book, he wrote a pro memoria which he sent to the officials of the European Monitoring Mission as well. But I repeat once again, for me they were not binding positions. He presented his views before the conflict actually arose in Bosnia-Herzegovina that his book is about, or the book that he published. I state once again possibly he did say things of that kind at a press conference in my presence, but they are not my own positions or views.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, he noted this at a press conference in the presence of you, and in the presence of Kordic, and in the presence of Kostroman, the three senior political people in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He said this probably in reply to the question that was put to him, and I have already told the Trial Chamber here that if the question is related to military matters, I would answer that a question of that kind. If the questions refer to civilian matters, then one of the civilian officials attending the conference would respond to them. Political questions were answered by the political representatives. So I don't know what context he said this in and I can't remember at the moment. If I were to see the document, perhaps that would refresh my memory. I do not doubt that he said it. I know that at that conference he stated that and he wrote about it but, once again, I would like to emphasise that I received orders from the chief of the main staff, and I didn't base myself on individual views.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, if we could take a look at Prosecutor's Exhibit 460.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, I will be referring to this document, so if I could give it to the respective booths. I think it would be helpful during the course of the translation. There is a French copy of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This was a document received by international agencies in May of 1993. I will not read all of it, General, and I realise it is in English. The first paragraph that I will read is on page 1. You can put it up, Mr. Usher, a little bit. It is on the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina HVO stationary, and it is entitled "Enabling People in Bosnia-Herzegovina Life in a Safer, Healthier, and Happier Surroundings." Just up a little bit, Mr. Usher. "What would be considered human and civilised is helping people interchange places where they live, apartments, family houses, or vocations no matter what intentions or causes make them do so." Can we turn the page, Mr. Usher, and we'll start with the first full paragraph beginning, "Muslims do not allow..." Just down a little bit. Thank you. "Muslims do not allow migrations or interchanging apartments and houses in Croat majority provinces no matter how much it is wanted on either of the sides in question. The reason for such an attitude is their hope that the increase of the population will make them the majority people not only in the municipalities with a slight Muslim majority but in those with Croat majority as well. For example, there are 25,000 Croats in Zenica. Most of them express the wish to move to Vitez or Busovaca, but the Muslim authorities in Zenica do not allow them too. They would rather keep them in Zenica where they are detained and harassed. Muslims of Vitez and Busovaca are ordered not to arrange the exchange of apartments or houses with Croats of Zenica. "Anyway, this pressure will have no affect. Croats will move into provinces where they are the majority of people." Just move it up a little bit more, and start with "For hundreds of years..." "For hundreds of years, Islam and the bysant Serbian culture have been imposed on Croats. What they felt as a pressure that made them immigrate from Bosnia-Herzegovina to Croatian, Western Europe, and America. "What exactly does it mean? About a thousand mosques were built in the past 50 years, all of them having high minarets. Approximately the same number of religious schools, mejtef, is built. Over 5.000 wide-range sound boxes are installed in them. The minarets are rather a dominating sign showing that the area under them belongs to Muslims, that that is a part of their religious heritage. Even in the smallest ethnically clean Muslim village (of a mixed one) there must be a mosque, a minaret, a powerful sound box. For three minutes, four times a day, you can hear the screaming of the Muslim prayer. For Croats and Serbs, melodically primitive Arabian song, which if imposed to be their future, frightens and scares. All this resulted in their revolt. "To be honest, churches have bells too but they toll for only 20 seconds a day. "Muslims never wonder if anyone else minds that the children sleep and elders rest. Teachers and professors stop their lectures during the prayers while their pupils laugh. Croats and Serbs whose houses are in the very vicinity of these buildings can hardly wait for the moment to move away. Muslims know that, so they are building more and more." Can we turn the page, Mr. Usher, to the bottom of the page beginning with the paragraph "If we add up all this evil..." "If we add to this evil all the incidents that happen in Travnik (burning down Croatian flags, murders, stealing property, burglaries into Croatian apartments and houses, and violence moving into Croatian apartments and houses) then the conclusion is evident: The mistrust and hatred between the two of the peoples is so high that it becomes a burden to live together; there has to be a way that could provide either of the two a safer, healthier, and happier surroundings. "It is clear by itself that human migrations should be considered for the benefit of both nations." Now, this was the view, this human migration view that was articulated in your presence at the press conference; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This view -- I wasn't able to see date of the document, but I know that he wrote the document and that Mr. Valenta expressed that view. However, I would like to say at this point that in a civil war, which existed in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the views of the UNHCR, which I spoke about, were not unified with regard to the resettlement of categories of the population. I explained to the Trial Chamber the problems that I myself was confronted with. I do not support this material, regardless of all the problems that we encountered in the field. So what Mr. Valenta wrote here, I don't support those views, and I think that on one occasion I stated that clearly to (redacted), in the course of our discussion. The document was written by Mr. Valenta and was probably sent to (redacted) as well, but I don't understand the language and didn't have the document in my own language to read through. I would just like to remind the Trial Chamber that the UNHCR had one set of views in Bosnia-Herzegovina controlled by the army of the Republika Srpska as with regard to the resettlement of the population, and they resettled the casualties of the conflict to areas controlled by the HVO forces and the BH army forces. It had other criteria in areas controlled by the BH army and the HVO, and that is that any movement of the population, even due to the dangers of war within that civil war, represented ethnic cleansing, whereas at the same time the International Red Cross and UNPROFOR advocated the theory of complete freedom of movement under wartime conditions of that kind. So this was a confusion of views and stands that I mentioned earlier on. I would like to say that May was a month when we once again had a joint command in operation of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, made up of General Petkovic and Halilovic, that is to say, at a lower level, and I myself and the commander of the 3rd Corps, Enver Hadzihasanovic, and this statement and this document, that is to say, it is a document by Mr. Anto Valenta.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You didn't agree with this view but you agreed with the views of Mayor Santic; didn't you? Isn't that what you said on direct-examination?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: With the views of Mayor Santic or with the majority of his views I did agree with, yes, because he had a rational approach to many questions and problems. I did not agree with all his views but I did agree with some of them. I worked in the direction of ensuring survival and life in the region. From Travnik, Zenica, and other areas, the Croats had been expelled and the Croats came to the Lasva pocket as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you agree with Santic's views on resettlement?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think that the views of Mr. Santic were radically different from Mr. Valenta's, and that within the context of a possible war and the situation that existed, he put forward certain views, but I know full well that for many Bosniak Muslims, Mr. Santic offered assistance and protection. He would send me information which enabled me to undertake measures, probably, not sufficiently efficacious, to provide protection for all the citizens of that Vitez area, including Muslims, Bosniaks, Romanies, Serbs, and everybody else who lived there, thanks to the information I got from Mr. Santic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you agree with Santic's view on resettlement?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could we know what it is, Mr. President? What --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: He knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this witness was the one that was dealing with Santic. The witness knows what Santic's views are. Let the witness answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We have to have a record, Mr. President. We can't have a secrete communication between anyone in the courtroom. There has to be a record of what is meant by a question and what is meant by the answer. That's elementary, absolutely elementary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, can you try to be more precise in the way you formulate your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did Santic have a view, a position, on the resettlement of the Muslim population and on the Croat population in the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already said that he had a diametrically contrary view to Mr. Valenta and that he endeavoured, and we saw this in the previous document, that whereas the -- while the conflict existed in Busovaca, the document that you showed me a moment ago, in Vitez a meeting was being held on the creation of a joint government, a Croatian and Bosniak Muslim government, and I know that he did everything in his power to ensure coexistence with the Bosniak Muslims. Now, whether at some stage when the situation was one of conflict, I don't know what his views were then, but as a consequence of the situation in the field, I don't know that. I do know that like me, he was against the evacuation of Romanies from the Vitez municipality, and that thanks to the information that he gave me, those people remained living in Vitez and the Romanies continued to live in the Vitez municipality, although they were to have been resettled elsewhere. For me, Mr. Santic did everything in the framework of his possibilities to ensure coexistence amongst all citizens living in the Vitez area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could go into private session briefly, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right then.
